question: Why does a Quebec calendar call the May Monday holiday Journée nationale des patriotes while a calendar elsewhere in Canada calls that date Victoria Day?
generated_answer:
You are here:

Why does a Quebec calendar call the May Monday holiday Journée nationale des patriotes while a calendar elsewhere in Canada calls that date Victoria Day? While it is Monday, May 20, 2019 for everyone in Canada, this date is known as Victoria Day in most of Canada and Journée nationale des patriotes in Quebec. You can check the name of this holiday on the Office of the Commissioner of Official Languages’ calendar tool. The reasons for this difference are historical. On the one hand, the sovereign’s birthday has been celebrated in Canada since the reign of Queen Victoria, who ruled over the United Kingdom, Canada and several other countries. The sovereign’s birthday was officially named Victoria Day in 1953. On the other hand, Quebec’s National Assembly designated the Monday before May 25 as Journée nationale des patriotes in 2003. This date commemorates the struggle and sacrifices of the patriots during the 1837-1838 rebellion. In short, these two holidays are not synonymous. You can consult the list of holidays in Canada to learn more. This article was written in collaboration with the Office of the Commissioner of Official Languages. Translation: Marie-Christine Cojan, Language Portal of Canada
